  {A : Type u} [inst_3 : CommRing A] [inst_4 : Algebra R A] [inst_5 : Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower R S A] {B : Type v}
  [inst_7 : CommRing B] [inst_8 : Algebra R B] [inst_9 : Algebra S B] [IsScalarTower R S B] (f : A →ₐ[S] B) (n : ℕ),
  (W.baseChange B).preΨ' n = Polynomial.map (↑f) ((W.baseChange A).preΨ' n)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, the $n$-th pre-normalized division polynomial $\Psi'_n$ of the base-changed Weierstrass curve over $B$ equals the polynomial obtained by applying the ring homomorphism $f$ to each coefficient of the $n$-th pre-normalized division polynomial $\Psi'_n$ of the base-changed Weierstrass curve over $A$.

items.informal_name: Base Change Compatibility of Division Polynomials for Weierstrass Curves
items.type:
∀ {R : Type r} {S : Type s} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] (W : WeierstrassCurve R) [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  {A : Type u} [inst_3 : CommRing A] [inst_4 : Algebra R A] [inst_5 : Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower R S A] {B : Type v}
  [inst_7 : CommRing B] [inst_8 : Algebra R B] [inst_9 : Algebra S B] [IsScalarTower R S B] (f : A →ₐ[S] B) (n : ℤ),
  (W.baseChange B).Ψ n = Polynomial.map (Polynomial.mapRingHom ↑f) ((W.baseChange A).Ψ n)
items.informal_description: For a Weierstrass curve $ W $ over a ring $ R $, an algebra homomorphism $ f : A 	o B $, and any integer $ n $, the division polynomial $ \Psi(n) $ of the base change $ W_{/B} $ satisfies $ \Psi_{W_{/B}}(n) = \Psi_{W_{/A}}(n)^{\phi_f} $, where $ \phi_f : R[A][X][Y] 	o R[B][X][Y] $ is the polynomial ring homomorphism induced by $ f $. This expresses compatibility between base change operations and division polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: φ-Polynomial Under Base Change via Ring Homomorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type r} {S : Type s} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] (W : WeierstrassCurve R) [inst_2 : Algebra R S]

  (W.baseChange B).φ n = Polynomial.map (Polynomial.mapRingHom ↑f) ((W.baseChange A).φ n)
items.informal_description: For any integer $n$, the $n$-th φ-polynomial of the base change of a Weierstrass curve $W$ over a commutative ring $R$ to a ring $B$ equals the image of the $n$-th φ-polynomial of the base change of $W$ to an intermediate ring $A$ under the polynomial map induced by the ring homomorphism $f : A 	o B$. items.informal_name: Base Change Compatibility of the Φ-Polynomial for Weierstrass Curves
items.type:
∀ {R : Type r} {S : Type s} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] (W : WeierstrassCurve R) [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  {A : Type u} [inst_3 : CommRing A] [inst_4 : Algebra R A] [inst_5 : Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower R S A] {B : Type v}
  [inst_7 : CommRing B] [inst_8 : Algebra R B] [inst_9 : Algebra S B] [IsScalarTower R S B] (f : A →ₐ[S] B) (n : ℤ),
  (W.baseChange B).Φ n = Polynomial.map (↑f) ((W.baseChange A).Φ n)
items.informal_description: For a Weierstrass curve $ W $ over a ring $ R $, an integer $ n $, and rings $ A $ and $ B $ equipped with algebra structures over $ R $, the Φ-polynomial of the base change of $ W $ to $ B $ equals the Φ-polynomial of the base change of $ W $ to $ A $ mapped through the ring homomorphism $ f : A → B $. Formally, $ (W_{/B})^{\Phi}_n = (W_{/A})^{\Phi}_n \circ f $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Kähler Differential Map with Derivations
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S] (A : Type u_2)
  (B : Type u_3) [inst_3 : CommRing A] [inst_4 : CommRing B] [inst_5 : Algebra R A] [inst_6 : Algebra A B]
  [inst_7 : Algebra S B] [inst_8 : Algebra R B] [inst_9 : IsScalarTower R A B] [inst_10 : IsScalarTower R S B]
  [inst_11 : SMulCommClass S A B] (x : A),
  (KaehlerDifferential.map R S A B) ((KaehlerDifferential.D R A) x) = (KaehlerDifferential.D S B) ((algebraMap A B) x)
items.informal_description: For any element $x$ in the $R$-algebra $A$, the Kähler differential map $\Omega_{A/R} \to \Omega_{B/S}$ sends the differential $dx$ to the differential of the image of $x$ under the algebra homomorphism $A \to B$, i.e., $\mathrm{map}(dx) = d(\mathrm{algebraMap}(x))$ in $\Omega_{B/S}$.
